## Overview

This spec defines the decoding of one DER X.509 v3 certificate (RFC 5280 section 4) into the fields a TLS client needs for path validation, as one function:

- **parse** -- decodes a certificate, checks it is strict DER and within the supported profile, and returns its fields, or an error naming the first problem found.

It decodes; it does not judge. Validity dates, signatures, CA status and names are returned, not checked: the `x509-verify` spec does that.

The supported profile is the one the Web PKI uses: signatures with ECDSA (P-256 and P-384), RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 and RSASSA-PSS (SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512) and Ed25519; public keys of those types; and the extensions path validation reads. An unknown extension is ignored unless it is critical.

**Out of scope:** BER and PEM input (PEM is the `pem` spec), certificate requests and CRLs, attribute certificates, X.509 v2 certificates, signature or key algorithms outside the tables below (SHA-1, MD5, DSA, P-521, Ed448, RSA-PSS keys), the content of extensions this spec does not list (certificate policies, CRL distribution points, authority information access, SCTs), name constraint forms
other than dNSName and iPAddress, IDNA conversion of names, and any check of a field's meaning (dates, key sizes, whether a key is on its curve).

## Types

Bytes values are given in test vectors as lowercase hex under the field name with `_hex` appended (`serial` is `serial_hex`, `ip_addresses` is `ip_addresses_hex`).

### Certificate

```pseudocode
type Certificate = {
  version: Int,                          // 1 or 3
  serial: Bytes,                         // content octets of the serialNumber INTEGER, as encoded
  signature_algorithm: String,           // see "Signature algorithms"
  issuer: Name,
  subject: Name,
  not_before: Int,                       // Unix seconds, UTC
  not_after: Int,                        // Unix seconds, UTC
  public_key: PublicKeyInfo,
  basic_constraints: BasicConstraints?,  // null when the extension is absent
  key_usage: [String]?,                  // set bit names in bit order; null when absent
  ext_key_usage: [String]?,              // dotted OIDs in encoded order; null when absent
  subject_alt_name: SubjectAltName?,     // null when absent
  authority_key_id: Bytes?,              // keyIdentifier of authorityKeyIdentifier; null when absent
  subject_key_id: Bytes?,                // subjectKeyIdentifier; null when absent
  name_constraints: NameConstraints?,    // null when absent
  tbs_certificate: Bytes,                // the whole TBSCertificate DER, tag and length included
  signature: Bytes,                      // signatureValue BIT STRING content after the unused-bits octet
}

type Name = {
  der: Bytes,                            // the whole Name DER (SEQUENCE OF RDN), tag and length included
  attributes: [Attribute],               // every AttributeTypeAndValue, RDNs flattened in encoded order
}

type Attribute = {
  oid: String,                           // dotted decimal, e.g. "2.5.4.3"
  name: String?,                         // "CN", "O", "OU" or "C" for 2.5.4.3, 2.5.4.10, 2.5.4.11, 2.5.4.6; else null
  value: String,                         // the decoded text
}

type PublicKeyInfo = {
  algorithm: String,                     // "rsa", "ec-p256", "ec-p384" or "ed25519"
  der: Bytes,                            // the whole SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, tag and length included
}

type BasicConstraints = { ca: Bool, path_len: Int? }
type SubjectAltName = { dns_names: [String], ip_addresses: [Bytes] }

type NameConstraints = {
  permitted_dns_names: [String],         // dNSName bases of permittedSubtrees, in encoded order, as encoded
  excluded_dns_names: [String],          // dNSName bases of excludedSubtrees
  permitted_ip_ranges: [Bytes],          // iPAddress bases of permittedSubtrees: address then mask, 8 or 32 bytes
  excluded_ip_ranges: [Bytes],           // iPAddress bases of excludedSubtrees
}
```

The key bytes are the `subjectPublicKey` BIT STRING content after its unused-bits octet: the uncompressed point for EC keys, 32 bytes for Ed25519, the `RSAPublicKey` DER for RSA. `der` is the form the `rsa-verify` spec takes.

### X509Error

```pseudocode
type X509Error =
  | InvalidEncoding             // not strict DER, or not the RFC 5280 structure
  | UnsupportedVersion          // a version other than v1 or v3
  | UnsupportedAlgorithm        // a well-formed algorithm identifier outside the supported tables
  | UnhandledCriticalExtension  // a critical extension this spec does not recognise
  | DuplicateExtension          // two extensions with the same OID
```

### Strict DER

Every TLV the parser reads, at any depth, must satisfy X.690 section 10 (DER); otherwise `InvalidEncoding`:

1. Single-octet tags only (no high-tag-number form). Definite lengths only; a length below 128 uses the short form; a long form has no leading zero octet and at most 4 length octets.
2. Every constructed value is exactly filled by its elements; nothing follows the outer Certificate.
3. INTEGER: at least one content octet, minimal two's complement (no leading `00` before a byte below `80`, no leading `ff` before a byte of `80` or more).
4. BOOLEAN: one content octet, `00` or `ff`.
5. BIT STRING: at least one octet; the first (unused-bit count) is 0 to 7, is 0 when there are no further octets, and the unused bits are zero.
6. OBJECT IDENTIFIER: at least one octet; no arc starts with `80`; the last octet has its top bit clear; no subidentifier is above 2^63 - 1 (Go's bound), in any OID the parser reads.
7. A field with a DEFAULT value is absent when it has that value: an explicit `[0] INTEGER 0` version, a `critical` of FALSE, a basicConstraints `cA` of FALSE, an RSASSA-PSS `saltLength` of 20 or `trailerField` of 1.
8. The AttributeTypeAndValue elements of a multi-valued RDN (a SET OF) are in ascending order of their encodings, compared as octet strings with the shorter padded with zero octets (X.690 section 11.6).

The extnValue of an extension this spec ignores is not decoded.

### Signature algorithms

`signature_algorithm` names the algorithm identifier. It is `UnsupportedAlgorithm` when the OID is not listed or the parameters are not as listed.

| `signature_algorithm` | OID | Parameters |
|---|---|---|
| `ecdsa-with-sha256` | 1.2.840.10045.4.3.2 | absent |
| `ecdsa-with-sha384` | 1.2.840.10045.4.3.3 | absent |
| `sha256-with-rsa-encryption` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.11 | NULL or absent |
| `sha384-with-rsa-encryption` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.12 | NULL or absent |
| `sha512-with-rsa-encryption` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.13 | NULL or absent |
| `rsassa-pss-sha256`, `-sha384`, `-sha512` | 1.2.840.113549.1.1.10 | RSASSA-PSS-params, below |
| `ed25519` | 1.3.101.112 | absent |

RFC 4055 section 5 requires a verifier to accept the PKCS #1 v1.5 identifiers with the NULL absent; real certificates do this.

RSASSA-PSS-params (RFC 4055 section 3.1) is `SEQUENCE { [0] EXPLICIT hashAlgorithm, [1] EXPLICIT maskGenAlgorithm, [2] EXPLICIT INTEGER saltLength, [3] EXPLICIT INTEGER trailerField }`, each optional, in that order. It is supported when:

- `hashAlgorithm` is present and is SHA-256 (2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.1), SHA-384 (.2) or SHA-512 (.3), with NULL or absent parameters;
- `maskGenAlgorithm` is present, is id-mgf1 (1.2.840.113549.1.1.8), and its parameter is the same hash's AlgorithmIdentifier (NULL or absent parameters);
- `saltLength` is present and equals the hash length (32, 48 or 64);
- `trailerField` is absent.

A missing parameters field, a missing `[0]`, `[1]` or `[2]` (whose defaults are SHA-1), another hash, another mask generation function or hash, another salt length, or a `trailerField` other than 1 is `UnsupportedAlgorithm`. Strict DER comes first: the whole parameters field is read before any of those checks, and it is `InvalidEncoding` unless it is a SEQUENCE of those tagged fields in order,
each holding exactly one element, `[0]` and `[1]` each an AlgorithmIdentifier (and `[1]`'s parameter too, when it is a SEQUENCE), `[2]` and `[3]` minimal INTEGERs other than their DEFAULTs 20 and 1.

### Public key algorithms

| `public_key.algorithm` | AlgorithmIdentifier | Key bytes |
|---|---|---|
| `rsa` | rsaEncryption 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1, NULL | a strict-DER `RSAPublicKey` SEQUENCE of two positive INTEGERs and nothing after it |
| `ec-p256` | id-ecPublicKey 1.2.840.10045.2.1, namedCurve prime256v1 1.2.840.10045.3.1.7 | 65 bytes, first byte `04` |
| `ec-p384` | id-ecPublicKey, namedCurve secp384r1 1.3.132.0.34 | 97 bytes, first byte `04` |
| `ed25519` | id-Ed25519 1.3.101.112, absent | 32 bytes |

Any other algorithm, curve or parameters (including absent RSA parameters) is `UnsupportedAlgorithm`. Key bytes of the wrong form, including a compressed point, or a BIT STRING with unused bits, are `InvalidEncoding`. Key sizes and point validity are not checked.

### Names

A Name is `SEQUENCE OF SET OF SEQUENCE { OBJECT IDENTIFIER, value }`. Every SET has at least one element. The value must be one of these string types; any other tag is `InvalidEncoding`:

| Tag | Type | Decoding (failure is `InvalidEncoding`) |
|---|---|---|
| `0c` | UTF8String | valid UTF-8 |
| `13` | PrintableString | only `A-Z a-z 0-9`, space and `' ( ) + , - . / : = ?` (no `*`, `&`, `@` or `_`) |
| `16` | IA5String | bytes `00` to `7f` |
| `14` | TeletexString | each byte is the code point of the same value (ISO 8859-1) |
| `1e` | BMPString | an even number of bytes, UTF-16BE code units, none a surrogate |
| `1c` | UniversalString | a multiple of 4 bytes, UTF-32BE code points, each a Unicode scalar value |

An empty Name (`30 00`) is valid. Names are compared by `der`, never by attributes.

### Validity

Each time is a UTCTime (tag `17`) of exactly `YYMMDDHHMMSSZ` or a GeneralizedTime (tag `18`) of exactly `YYYYMMDDHHMMSSZ`: digits, then `Z`. No fractional seconds and no offsets. A UTCTime year `YY` of 50 or more is `19YY`, otherwise `20YY`. Month 1 to 12, a day that exists in that month and year, hour 0 to 23, minute and second 0 to 59. Either type is accepted for any year. The result is seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, negative before it.

### Extensions

Each Extension is `SEQUENCE { OBJECT IDENTIFIER, BOOLEAN critical DEFAULT FALSE, OCTET STRING extnValue }`. The recognised extensions and the decoding of their extnValue, which must be exactly one DER value:

| OID | Extension | Decoding |
|---|---|---|
| 2.5.29.19 | basicConstraints | `SEQUENCE { cA BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, pathLenConstraint INTEGER OPTIONAL }`; a negative pathLen, or one above 2^63 - 1, is `InvalidEncoding` |
| 2.5.29.15 | keyUsage | a BIT STRING; bit `i` (bit 0 is the top bit of the first content octet) names, in order: `digital-signature`, `content-commitment`, `key-encipherment`, `data-encipherment`, `key-agreement`, `key-cert-sign`, `crl-sign`, `encipher-only`, `decipher-only`; bits beyond 8 are ignored; none of the nine set is `InvalidEncoding` |
| 2.5.29.37 | extKeyUsage | `SEQUENCE SIZE (1..MAX) OF OBJECT IDENTIFIER` |
| 2.5.29.17 | subjectAltName | `SEQUENCE SIZE (1..MAX) OF GeneralName`; see below |
| 2.5.29.35 | authorityKeyIdentifier | `SEQUENCE { [0] keyIdentifier OPTIONAL, [1] authorityCertIssuer OPTIONAL, [2] serial OPTIONAL }` in that order; only `[0]` is returned |
| 2.5.29.14 | subjectKeyIdentifier | an OCTET STRING |
| 2.5.29.30 | nameConstraints | `SEQUENCE { permittedSubtrees [0] OPTIONAL, excludedSubtrees [1] OPTIONAL }`; see below |

GeneralName is a context-specific tag 0 to 8. `[2]` dNSName (primitive) is returned in `dns_names` as text and must be bytes `00` to `7f`; `[7]` iPAddress (primitive) is returned in `ip_addresses` and must be 4 or 16 bytes. The others are well-formed TLVs and are skipped: `[0]`, `[3]`, `[4]` and `[5]` must be constructed, `[1]`, `[6]` and `[8]` primitive, and `[4]` (EXPLICIT Name) holds exactly one element.

nameConstraints (RFC 5280 section 4.2.1.10) holds `[0]`, `[1]` or both, in that order; it is `InvalidEncoding` with neither. Each is a constructed `SEQUENCE SIZE (1..MAX) OF GeneralSubtree`, and each GeneralSubtree is a SEQUENCE holding exactly one GeneralName (the `base`): a `minimum` or `maximum` is `InvalidEncoding`, as RFC 5280 forbids them. The base is checked like a subjectAltName GeneralName, and then:

- `[2]` dNSName must be bytes `00` to `7f`; after removing one leading `.`, it is empty or a sequence of labels separated by `.`, each label of 1 or more bytes from `21` to `7e`. It is returned as encoded, leading `.` included. Otherwise `InvalidEncoding`.
- `[7]` iPAddress is an address followed by a mask of the same length, 8 or 32 bytes. The mask is a run of 1 bits followed only by 0 bits. Otherwise `InvalidEncoding`.
- Any other form is skipped. If the extension is critical, a skipped form is `UnhandledCriticalExtension`, raised after the whole value has been checked for `InvalidEncoding`.

## Functions

### parse

```pseudocode
parse(der: Bytes) -> Certificate | X509Error
```

**Parameters:**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `der` | Bytes | yes | One DER certificate |

**Returns:** the Certificate, or the X509Error of the first failing step.

**Algorithm.** The steps run in order and the first failure is returned. Within a step, the checks run in the order written. Strict DER is checked on every TLV as it is read.

1. **Structure.** `der` is one `SEQUENCE { tbsCertificate SEQUENCE, signatureAlgorithm SEQUENCE, signatureValue BIT STRING }` and nothing after it. The TBSCertificate's elements are split (each must be a well-formed TLV filling it exactly). Otherwise `InvalidEncoding`.
2. **Version.** If the first TBS element is `[0]`, it holds exactly one INTEGER `v`: `v = 0` is `InvalidEncoding` (DEFAULT), `v = 2` is version 3, anything else is `UnsupportedVersion`. With no `[0]` the version is 1.
3. **Serial.** The next element is an INTEGER. Its content octets are `serial`, of any sign and length.
4. **Signature algorithm.** The next element is a SEQUENCE. Both it and `signatureAlgorithm` are `SEQUENCE { OBJECT IDENTIFIER, one optional element }`; the two must be byte-for-byte equal (RFC 5280 section 4.1.1.2). Otherwise `InvalidEncoding`. Then classify it by the table: `UnsupportedAlgorithm` or `InvalidEncoding` as described there.
5. **Issuer.** The next element is a Name.
6. **Validity.** The next element is `SEQUENCE { notBefore, notAfter }`.
7. **Subject.** The next element is a Name.
8. **SubjectPublicKeyInfo.** The next element is `SEQUENCE { AlgorithmIdentifier, BIT STRING }`. Classify the algorithm (`UnsupportedAlgorithm`), then check the BIT STRING has no unused bits and the key bytes have the listed form (`InvalidEncoding`).
9. **Unique identifiers.** Optional `[1]` then `[2]`, each a primitive BIT STRING; ignored. In a version 1 certificate either is `InvalidEncoding`.
10. **Extensions.** Optional `[3]` holding exactly one SEQUENCE of at least one Extension. In a version 1 certificate it is `InvalidEncoding`. For each Extension in order: check its structure (`InvalidEncoding`); if its OID equals an earlier one's, `DuplicateExtension`; if the OID is recognised, decode extnValue (`InvalidEncoding`, or `UnhandledCriticalExtension` for a critical nameConstraints
with a skipped form); otherwise, if critical, `UnhandledCriticalExtension`; otherwise ignore it.
11. **End.** No TBS element may remain (`InvalidEncoding`). The signatureValue BIT STRING has no unused bits (`InvalidEncoding`); its remaining octets are `signature`.

## Behavioral Contracts

### parse()

**MUST:**

1. MUST apply the strict-DER rules to every structure it decodes and return `InvalidEncoding` on any violation, including trailing bytes, BER lengths and encoded DEFAULT values.
2. MUST return the first error in step order, so an input with several faults has exactly one expected error.
3. MUST accept a serial number that is zero, negative or longer than 20 octets, and return its content octets unchanged. RFC 5280 section 4.1.2.2 requires CAs to issue positive serials of at most 20 octets but tells users to handle non-conforming ones gracefully; the serial is only an identifier here.
4. MUST require the signature algorithm inside the TBSCertificate to equal the outer one byte for byte.
5. MUST return `UnhandledCriticalExtension` for a critical extension it does not recognise, and ignore a non-critical one without decoding it.
6. MUST detect a duplicate extension OID among all extensions, recognised or not (RFC 5280 section 4.2).
7. MUST return `tbs_certificate` exactly as encoded, since it is the signed message.
8. MUST NOT use any attribute of a Name for anything but reporting it; names are matched by `der`.

## Test Vectors

`der_hex` is the input, lowercase hex. A success is a `result` holding the Certificate, with Bytes fields as `_hex` strings and absent extensions as `null`; a failure is an `error`. Tags name the source (`real`, `generated`, `malformed`), the certificate, the algorithms and the feature.

### Sources

- `real` vectors (8 successes, 4 errors) are published certificates: ISRG Root X1, ISRG Root X2, Let's Encrypt R10 and E5, and ISRG Root X2 cross-signed by ISRG Root X1, from https://letsencrypt.org/certificates/ (the DER files under `letsencrypt.org/certs/`); GTS Root R4 from `pki.goog/repo/certs/gtsr4.der`; Amazon Root CA 3 from `amazontrust.com/repository/AmazonRootCA3.cer`; DigiCert Global
  Root G2 and DigiCert Global Root CA from `cacerts.digicert.com`. All were fetched on 2026-10-22. DigiCert Global Root CA is self-signed with SHA-1 and expects `UnsupportedAlgorithm`; the other real errors are mutations of ISRG Root X2 (truncation, BER lengths).
- `generated` vectors (33) are certificates made for this spec. The keys (P-256, P-384, RSA-2048, RSA-4096, Ed25519) were generated with pyca/cryptography; the DER was written by a script so that each field, string type and extension variant is chosen exactly; each is signed by its issuer's key. They cover every signature algorithm and key type, v1 certificates, serial-number edge cases, each
  extension's variants (name constraints with dNSName, iPAddress and skipped subtrees), every string type and a multi-valued RDN, time encodings at their boundaries, and unique identifiers.
- `malformed` vectors (66) are constructed error cases, one fault each except those tagged `precedence`, which combine two to fix the order of the steps.
- Every expected value was computed by a pure-Python implementation of this spec with its own DER reader. Every success was compared field by field with the certificate loader of pyca/cryptography 50.0.2 and agreed, except `teletex-latin-1`, which that loader refuses. Of the 70 error vectors the loader also refuses 46. It accepts the other 24 because it does not apply this spec's rules: the
  algorithm tables (SHA-1, ecdsa-with-SHA512, PSS parameters, P-521, absent RSA key parameters, compressed points), the equality of the two signature algorithm fields, extensions or unique identifiers in a v1 certificate, empty extensions, keyUsage or subjectAltName, a non-ASCII dNSName, unknown critical extensions (left to its verifier), a critical nameConstraints with an rfc822Name subtree
  (which it supports), a GeneralSubtree with a maximum, a dNSName subtree with an empty label, a pathLenConstraint of 2^63, an OID arc of 2^63 or more, and unused bits in the signature.

## Edge Cases

- **Negative or zero serial.** Accepted; `serial_hex` keeps the two's-complement bytes (`fb2e` for -1234, `00` for 0).
- **21-octet serial.** A positive 20-octet value with its top bit set needs a leading `00`; accepted.
- **Explicit version v1 (`a0 03 02 01 00`).** `InvalidEncoding`, not version 1: DER forbids encoding the DEFAULT.
- **Version v2 or v4.** `UnsupportedVersion`, checked before the algorithm, so a v2 certificate with SHA-1 is `UnsupportedVersion`.
- **basicConstraints `30 00`.** Valid: `{ca: false, path_len: null}`. With `01 01 00` inside it is `InvalidEncoding`.
- **pathLen without cA.** Returned as encoded; `x509-verify` ignores it because such a certificate is not a CA.
- **keyUsage `03 01 00`.** No bits set: `InvalidEncoding`. Trailing zero bits beyond the last set bit are tolerated (many issuers emit them); the unused bits must still be zero.
- **dNSName with a non-ASCII byte.** `InvalidEncoding`; a dNSName is IA5String. An empty or malformed name is returned as is; matching it is `x509-verify`'s job.
- **nameConstraints `[0]` holding only an rfc822Name.** Non-critical: returned with four empty lists. Critical: `UnhandledCriticalExtension`.
- **A dNSName subtree of `""` or `.`.** Valid; it covers every name.
- **SubjectAltName with only an email or URI.** Returned with empty `dns_names` and `ip_addresses`.
- **Empty subject with a critical subjectAltName.** Valid (RFC 5280 section 4.2.1.6).
- **A duplicate extension whose second copy is malformed.** `DuplicateExtension`: the duplicate check comes before the value is decoded.
- **An unknown critical extension repeated.** `UnhandledCriticalExtension`, from the first copy.
- **`notAfter` of `99991231235959Z`.** RFC 5280's "no well-defined expiration": 253402300799.
- **GeneralizedTime before 2050 and UTCTime of `500101000000Z`.** Accepted: -631152000 for 1950-01-01.
- **TeletexString with byte `c9`.** Decoded as U+00C9 (`\u00c9` in the JSON of the vector).
- **PrintableString containing `*` or `&`.** `InvalidEncoding`, though some issuers have used them.
- **sha1WithRSAEncryption.** `UnsupportedAlgorithm`, including on a self-signed root, whose signature a verifier never checks.

## Implementation Notes

- **Write one strict TLV reader** that returns tag, content start and end, and use it for everything; most of the errors are its errors. Check `start + length <= end` before slicing: a truncated input is a length that overruns its parent.
- **Keep byte ranges, not copies.** `tbs_certificate`, the Name `der` values and the SPKI `der` are slices of the input. Path building compares names by these bytes, and signature verification hashes `tbs_certificate`.
- **Compare algorithm identifiers as bytes** first (step 4), then decode one. The PKCS #1 v1.5 identifiers have two accepted encodings each (`300d06092a864886f70d01010b0500` and `300b06092a864886f70d01010b` for SHA-256).
- **Unknown extensions are cheap.** Their extnValue is an OCTET STRING whose content is never parsed, so a malformed unknown non-critical extension is not an error.
- **Do not decode lazily.** A parser that decodes extensions on first access reports errors late or never; this spec requires every listed check during `parse`.
- **Text.** Return attribute values as Unicode text. A PrintableString check is a character class test; UTF-8 must be validated, not trusted.
- **Times.** Convert with a days-from-civil computation, not a local-time library: the result is UTC and may be negative.

## References

- [RFC 5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html) -- certificate structure (4.1), serial numbers (4.1.2.2), validity and time encodings (4.1.2.5), extensions (4.2), basic constraints (4.2.1.9), key usage (4.2.1.3), subject alternative name (4.2.1.6), name constraints (4.2.1.10).
- [ITU-T X.690](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-X.690) -- DER (section 10), SET OF ordering (11.6), BIT STRING named bits (11.2).
- [RFC 4055](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055.html) -- RSASSA-PSS-params (3.1) and the SHA-2 RSA identifiers (5).
- [RFC 3279](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3279.html) -- `rsaEncryption` and its NULL parameters (2.3.1).
- [RFC 5480](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5480.html) -- elliptic curve SubjectPublicKeyInfo (2).
- [RFC 5758](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5758.html) -- ECDSA signature identifiers with absent parameters (3.2).
- [RFC 8410](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8410.html) -- Ed25519 identifiers and keys (3, 4).
- [RFC 4519](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4519.html) -- the CN, O, OU and C attribute types.
- [Let's Encrypt chains of trust](https://letsencrypt.org/certificates/) -- ISRG Root X1 and X2 and their intermediates.
